title: Secretary of State of Idaho

context.text: Neither primary was contested: incumbent Phil McGrane (R) advanced with 188,089 votes and Shawn Keenan (D) with 43,133 votes on May 19, 2026.
After statewide filing closed, the Idaho Capital Sun reported that McGrane and Keenan would face off in November; The Green Papers lists only the two.

candidates.name: Phil McGrane
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the May 19 Republican primary.

priorities.text: Protect elections: his campaign cites running the largest election in Idaho history and strengthening safeguards.
Protect lands, saying he trained as a wildland firefighter and works with timber, mining, agriculture and recreation interests.
Reduce red tape and increase transparency, including a redesigned VoteIdaho.gov and modernized campaign-finance and lobbyist reporting systems.

statements.quote: strengthening Idaho's work to verify voter eligibility and ensure that only U.S. citizens vote in Idaho elections.
statements.context: On helping implement Gov. Brad Little's 'Only Citizens Will Vote' Act, from his campaign site.

record.text: Partnered with Idaho's 44 county clerks to adopt the '12 Principles of Idaho Elections,' a statement of commitment to accessible, secure, locally run elections.
Helped implement the 'Only Citizens Will Vote' Act and worked with the Legislature on stronger voter ID protections and voter-roll maintenance (his campaign's description).

candidates.researchNotes: Record items rely on his campaign's account and the office's 12 Principles page; individual rules or certifications were not itemized.

candidates.name: Shawn Keenan
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the May 19 Democratic primary.
candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia survey or public platform statements were found for Keenan; only his nomination and 2022 run are documented.

sources.title: Idaho's Republican state officials are all running for re-election. Who are the other candidates?
The Green Papers: Idaho 2026 General Election

researchNotes: Slate: the Idaho Secretary of State's candidate portal is script-driven and could not be read; the slate rests on the Idaho Capital Sun and The Green Papers. Primary vote counts and details sourced only to Ballotpedia (blocked) were not re-verified; other sources show slightly different counts. Keenan's depth is limited by lack of public material.
